chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Mansoor ibn Hazim, on the authority of Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon them both).
He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand words, each of which opens up to one thousand words.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the thousand words taught to Imam Ali by the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal illustrates the concept of 'Ilf' (conciseness with depth) in Imam Ali’s (AS) knowledge, where a single word encapsulates a vast semantic field, reflecting the comprehensive nature of divine wisdom transmitted to the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores the Shia belief in the Imam’s unique capacity to interpret the Quran’s inner meanings, linking the Prophet’s teaching to the broader tradition of esoteric knowledge (Ilm al-Batin).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-40 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Mansoor ibn Hazim, on the authority of Abi Hamzih al-Somali, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB), “
God’s Prophet (MGB) taught Ali (MGB) one-thousand words which open up to the doors to all words (each of which open up to the doors to all words).”
